title: Refuge-fiducia: not formal when faith is precise; included in living faith’s aggregate
source_text: XCVIII. Quod spectat fiduciam primo modo acceptam, nempe pro actu illo, quo Deo innitimur & ad eum confugimus, ut vitam & salutem ab eo consequamur, de illa idem dicendum videtur, quod de amore jam dictum: nempe eam non esse formalem fidei actum, si fides praecise sumatur, & prout a caeteris virtutibus omnibus distinguitur, ac eis opponitur. Sed si fides sumatur pro aggregato illo variorum actuum, qui fidei vivae, & per dilectionem operantis nomine designantur, dubitari non debet quin fiducia haec partem ejus faciat, & ea includatur.
pass_a_gloss: As to trust taken in the first mode, namely for that act by which we lean upon God and flee to him, that we may obtain life and salvation from him, the same seems to be said of it which has already been said of love: namely that it is not a formal act of faith, if faith is taken precisely, and as it is distinguished from all the remaining virtues and opposed to them. But if faith is taken for that aggregate of various acts which are designated by the name of living faith working through love, it ought not to be doubted that this trust makes a part of it and is included in it.
pass_b_english: Refuge-fiducia (leaning on God / fleeing to him for life and salvation) follows the same rule as love.
Take faith precisely (apart from other virtues) → not faith’s formal act.
Take faith as living faith working through love’s aggregate → this fiducia is included as a part.
